name: b43-fwcutter
desc: Extract firmware from Braodcom 43xx driver files
why: Extracts Broadcom wireless firmware from driver files, a real firmware-taking-apart exercise tied to old hardware.

brief.what_it_is: b43-fwcutter is a command-line tool, installed as the executable b43-fwcutter, described in its Homebrew metadata as extracting firmware from Broadcom 43xx driver files. Per the brew description it takes Broadcom wireless driver files as input and produces firmware images that the Linux b43 driver can load. I could not confirm this from the page I read, which is the b43 driver documentation rather than the tool's own documentation.
brief.why_it_exists: The b43 driver needs proprietary Broadcom firmware files, usually in /lib/firmware/, before it can upload them to the card. The homepage says this directly: 'You need to have firmware files (usually in /lib/firmware/) so b43(legacy) can upload them to the card and run properly.' The tool exists to produce those files from the driver material; the homepage does not name it.
brief.how_it_works: Not described on the page I read. The brew scout note says it extracts firmware from driver files. I did not find the mechanism in the homepage text.

commands_seen.context: From the b43 driver page, not from b43-fwcutter docs: checks which Broadcom (vendor 14e4) PCI device is present, so you can look up whether your chip is supported before dealing with firmware.

brief.install_notes: Nothing about installing b43-fwcutter was on the page I read. The page does say the b43 driver needs firmware files in /lib/firmware/ and that some Broadcom chips only appear after the ssb kernel module is loaded. The Homebrew formula's executable is b43-fwcutter. Note that the brew description spells Broadcom as 'Braodcom'; the writer should use the correct spelling.
brief.standout: The scout note calls it a real firmware-taking-apart exercise tied to old hardware. That is the scout's view, not something I confirmed in the tool's own text. The b43 page itself is a reminder that this firmware is needed for hardware that is still in use.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage is the Linux Wireless b43 driver page and shows no release date, last commit, or maintenance note for b43-fwcutter. It mentions an old website copy and says content was removed for relicensing, but says nothing about the fwcutter tool.
brief.caveats: The homepage I was given is the b43 driver documentation, not a page for b43-fwcutter, so most of the tool-specific brief is unverified and comes from the brew description and scout note. I did not find the tool's own README or repository. The page also notes that the content was removed for relicensing and that a copy is kept on an old site. Among the supported chips listed, many are marked 'not tested' or 'partially', and 802.11n features are limited. Using the firmware may involve Broadcom's licensing terms, which I did not check.
